Commentary.Commentary: Right then, we have had three T20Is but there are still a couple of more matches to go. With that said, the caravan now moves to the west of the Atlantic Ocean to the United States of America for the final two matches. The 4th T20I will be played on Saturday, the 12th of August in Lauderhill, Florida and will begin at 8 pm IST (2.30 pm GMT). Our build-up though will begin a lot sooner. Do join us for all the exciting action. Take care and goodbye!

Hardik Pandya, the skipper of India, says that it was a very important win. Adds that they had spoken as a group about these three games being exciting. Mentions that two losses do not change much for them. Feels that it is important to show that they mean business when it comes to such games. Shares that since Nicholas Pooran had not come out to bat, it allowed him to use his spinners. Credits the spinners for their fantastic effort and adds that Mukesh Kumar and Arshdeeep Singh bowled well as well. States they need to take responsibility while playing with seven batters. Ends by saying that it is important to have someone like Suryakumar Yadav in the team who can take responsibility.

Rovman Powell, the captain of West Indies says that they were about 10-15 runs short and it turned out to be a good batting wicket. Adds that they did well with the bat but lost their way a bit in the middle overs. Mentions that looking back, Nicholas Pooran could have been sent up the order but they wanted to give Johnson Charles a chance and in the end, they were a few runs short. Adds that they bowled a lot of pace-on deliveries and it would have been better to take pace off but they have a few days in hand and will look to bounce back later.

Suryakumar Yadav is the PLAYER OF THE MATCH for his stellar knock of 83 runs from 44 balls. He says that it was really important to be himself. Adds that the team management wanted him to bat as much as possible. On his unorthodox strokes, he says that he has practiced these strokes a lot at home. Also says that he loves playing these strokes and is happy with how things went. On his chemistry with Tilak Varma, he says that both understand each other well. Adds that the way Tilak batted gave him confidence. Mentions that it was a great inning from Tilak. Shares that Hardik Pandya had spoken in the meeting about someone needing to put their hands up and he is happy to do that.
The Presentation ceremony...

Earlier in the game, Rovman Powell won the toss and opted to bat and the openers got West Indies off to a fairly decent start. The innings fell apart a bit in the middle overs with Brandon King holding up one end and the dismissal of Nicholas Pooran put the brakes on the innings. It was then a fiery cameo by the skipper Rovman Powell in the back end of the innings that took them to 159 runs. For India, the spinners bowled for most of the innings with the pacers bowling the first two and death overs. Axar Patel completed his quota at the halfway mark and bowled well but Kuldeep Yadav picked up three wickets and allowed the visitors to control the middle phase. Coming to the chase, India came out with an aggressive intent and even though they lost a couple of early wickets, they had more than enough firepower to get the win.

West Indies will be a tad disappointed with that bowling effort but they were treated to some exquisite batting from Suryakumar Yadav. Obed McCoy picked up a wicket early but was torn apart in his two overs and it was a similar story with Romario Shepherd who too went for plenty. The spinners bowled decently well but simply didn't have the wickets in the middle overs. Alzarri Joseph was the only bowler who trouble the Indian batters and picked up a couple of wickets as well but it wasn't enough.

The series is well and truly alive as India make it 2-1 after having gone 2-0 behind! Under the immense pressure of losing the five-match series in the third game itself, India have pulled off a statement victory here. Chasing 160, the highest score of this series, India got off to a quick start but did lose Yashasvi Jaiswal in the first over itself. Suryakumar Yadav came in and played a few shots but Shubman Gill once again disappointed getting out in the Powerplay. After that, the visitors went on a rampage with Yadav showing no mercy to the Windies bowlers and Tilak Varma playing another fine supporting knock. Yadav got a quick fifty and got out on 83 but Varma kept on his impressive showing and along with skipper Hardik Pandya, took his side over the line, remaining unbeaten on 49.

SIX! THAT'S IT! Hardik Pandya goes down the ground for a maximum and Tilak Varma will remain unbeaten on 49! Rovman Powell bowls another off cutter, on a length, on off, Hardik Pandya gets it in his slot and does not miss out. Picks the bones out of it and clears the long off fence easily for a maximum. India win by 7 wickets!

Commentary.Commentary: That one zipped through! Good length outside off at 145 clicks, shaping away a bit. Shubman Gill looks to reach out and cut but is unable to reach it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Alzarri Joseph to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches this one up on the stumps at 146 clicks, classy flick from Shubman Gill but straight to the man at mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Alzarri Joseph to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it short of a length in the channel and at 138 clicks. The ball zips off the deck and moves away as Shubman Gill simply leaves it alone.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Alzarri Joseph to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length around off, punched off the back foot in front of point for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Alzarri Joseph to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts off on a good length around off, moving away a little. Suryakumar Yadav looks to drive on the up but gets a big inside edge onto the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Alzarri Joseph to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Alzarri Joseph is introduced into the attack now.
Just away from the fielder! Nicely flighted around off, holding in the surface a bit. Suryakumar Yadav is undone due to this and drives it uppishly to the right of extra cover for a run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Akeal Hosein to Suryakumar Yadav, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Drifted very full on the pads, Suryakumar Yadav wrists it away through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Akeal Hosein to Suryakumar Yadav, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Gets it away! Flighted one outside off, and the length is pulled back a bit. Suryakumar Yadav does get beaten in the flight a bit but manages to slap it away over cover-point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Akeal Hosein to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: No ball! Nicely bowled! Full and outside off, turning away quickly, Suryakumar Yadav looks for the lofted drive over covers but is well beaten. Oh, no! Akeal Hosein has committed a cardinal sin here as he has overstepped and a Free Hit will now follow.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Akeal Hosein to Suryakumar Yadav, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: This one comes in with the arm on leg stump, Suryakumar Yadav rocks back and pushes it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Akeal Hosein to Suryakumar Yadav, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on the stumps, pushed down to long off for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Akeal Hosein to Shubman Gill, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted, a bit fuller and outside off, Shubman Gill caresses it toward cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Akeal Hosein to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It will be the spin of Akeal Hosein from the other end. It has gotten a bit gloomy at the Providence Stadium but let's hope the rain stays away. The DLS par score for India at the end of 5 overs is 35.

SIX! Oh, my! What a start to the chase we have had here, 16 runs and a wicket off the first over. This is banged in short over leg stump by Obed McCoy, Suryakumar Yadav just gets inside the line and pulls it well over the fine leg fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Obed McCoy to Suryakumar Yadav, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Suryakumar Yadav is up and running in style. Overpitched on the pads, Yadav flicks it aerially using his wrists well over wide mid-wicket and picks up a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Obed McCoy to Suryakumar Yadav, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Suryakumar Yadav walks out to the centre.

OUT! TAKEN! Yashasvi Jaiswal's T20I debut is short-lived as he departs on the second ball that he faces and India lose an early wicket. Served on a good length by Obed McCoy and on off stump, Jaiswal looks to get under it and tries to hit it hard over long on. Jaiswal ends up lifting it a mile high and just over wide mid on. Alzarri Joseph from mid on circles around and takes a very good catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Alzarri Joseph b Obed McCoy
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Obed McCoy to Yashasvi Jaiswal, OUT! c Alzarri Joseph b Obed McCoy.

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Back of a length around leg, Shubman Gill looks to get it away but misses. The ball comes off the thigh pad and goes to square leg. They pick up a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Obed McCoy to Shubman Gill, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely played and Shubman Gill is off the mark as well! Slightly shorter outside off, Gill waits for it and opens the face of the bat late to slice it wide of short third for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Obed McCoy to Shubman Gill, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Yashasvi Jaiswal is off the mark right away in T20I cricket! Obed McCoy starts with a short ball angled at the body, Jaiswal stays back and pulls it firmly to deep square leg for a single. India are up and running in the chase!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Obed McCoy to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.
